part.text: Corporate tax cuts don't reliably boost long-term job growth because hiring decisions are driven primarily by consumer demand, credit conditions, and regulations—not the effective tax rate corporations pay. Empirical evidence from major tax cuts (2017 US Tax Cuts and Jobs Act) shows most benefits flowed to shareholders via stock buybacks and dividends, not wages or employment. Studies consistently find minimal correlation between lower corporate rates and sustained job creation or wage growth. Meanwhile, reduced revenue can force cutbacks in public investments (education, infrastructure, R&D) that actually expand workforce productivity. Job growth responds to aggregate economic conditions and worker purchasing power; passing tax benefits through to workers has historically been limited and short-lived.
